## Massachusetts (MA)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ma/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Massachusetts offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is a standalone teaching license. SEI training is mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 10.5% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2017.

SEI notes: SEI endorsement required for core academic teachers, administrators, and (since July 1, 2021) vocational educators. Statutory backbone: LOOK Act (2017); endorsement framework codified at 603 CMR 7.14(1).

History:
- 1971-11-04: Massachusetts enacts first-in-nation transitional bilingual education mandate (Ch. 1005 of the Acts of 1971) — An Act Providing for the Equal Educational Opportunities of Children with Limited Speaking Ability of the English Language (codified at M.G.L. c. 71A) required districts enrolling 20 or more students of the same non-English language background to provide transitional bilingual education (TBE) in that language. Massachusetts was the first U.S. state to mandate bilingual instruction; the statute became the template cited in the federal Bilingual Education Act's later reauthorizations and in subsequent state TBE laws.
- 2002-11-05: Voters pass Question 2 — English-only mandate replaces TBE (Ch. 386 of the Acts of 2002) — Ballot Question 2 ("English Language Education in Public Schools"), modeled on California Proposition 227 (1998) and Arizona Proposition 203 (2000) and bankrolled by Ron Unz's English for the Children campaign, passed roughly 68%–32%. It rewrote M.G.L. c. 71A to repeal the 1971 transitional-bilingual mandate and require Sheltered English Immersion (SEI) for nearly all EL students, with narrowly drawn parental waivers. Effective for the 2003-2004 school year. The mandate remained in force until partially repealed by the 2017 LOOK Act, which restored district choice over program model.
- 2011-06-14: U.S. DOJ / MA DESE settlement triggers RETELL and the SEI endorsement framework — Following a federal investigation that found Massachusetts's pre-existing "Category 1-4" SEI training out of compliance with the Equal Educational Opportunities Act and the Castañeda v. Pickard standard, the U.S. Department of Justice and MA DESE entered a settlement agreement. DESE responded by launching RETELL (Rethinking Equity and Teaching for English Language Learners) in 2012 — a statewide initiative that promulgated 603 CMR 7.14(1), the Sheltered English Immersion endorsement, and required core-academic teachers and administrators of ELs to obtain it on a phased schedule. RETELL is the operational backbone the LOOK Act later codified.
- 2017-11-22: Massachusetts enacts the LOOK Act (Ch. 138 of the Acts of 2017) — An Act Relative to Language Opportunity for Our Kids (LOOK Act) repealed the 2002 English-only mandate and authorized districts to choose program models including dual language, two-way immersion, transitional bilingual, SEI, and other research-based approaches. The act also authorized the State Seal of Biliteracy and codified the SEI endorsement framework binding core-academic teachers of ELs (later operationalized at 603 CMR 7.14(1)).
- 2017-11-22: Massachusetts authorizes State Seal of Biliteracy — The LOOK Act simultaneously authorized the Massachusetts State Seal of Biliteracy. DESE administers the credential for high-school graduates demonstrating proficiency in English plus one or more world languages.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2021-07-01: SEI endorsement requirement extended to vocational educators — Effective 2021-07-01, MA DESE extended the SEI endorsement requirement (already binding on core-academic teachers and administrators of ELs) to vocational educators serving ELs. This expanded the operative scope of `sei.mandatedForAllTeachers = true` in MA without changing the underlying coding.
- 2026-05-07: Re-verified against current DESE sources — Bilingual reclassified standalone → add-on; ESL reclassified add-on → standalone (DESE lists Bilingual only as an endorsement and ESL as an Academic PreK-12 license). SEI mandate scope confirmed extended to vocational educators effective July 2021 under the LOOK Act. elPercent updated 10.0 → 10.5 (NCES fall 2021).
- 2026-05-08: Re-audit (history events captured) — Re-audited the prior 2026-05-07 verification. No coding changes; this pass added LOOK Act enactment (2017), Seal of Biliteracy authorization, and the 2021 SEI vocational-educator extension to the history log per the §3a history-capture emphasis.

## Michigan (MI)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/mi/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Michigan offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 6.4% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2018.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual Education endorsement is language-specific (codes YA-YT, 17 languages). Standard 1.1 of the 2017 Bilingual Education Preparation Standards requires ACTFL Oral Proficiency Interview at Advanced Low or higher in both English and the target language. MTTC Bilingual Education exam also required.

ELD notes: ESL endorsement (code NS). Earned via an approved Educator Preparation Provider as either the initial endorsement on a teaching certificate or as an add-on, plus passage of the MTTC ESL exam. ESL preparation standards (2017, rev. 2024) do not require a separate language-proficiency exam.

SEI notes: Michigan does not mandate SEI training for all teachers. Per Michigan Law 380.1233(1) and the MDE ESL & Bilingual Placement Guide (2024), only teachers serving as the primary EL provider in ESL, sheltered English, bilingual, newcomer, or dual-language programs must hold the NS or Y_ endorsement.

History:
- 2017-01-01: Bilingual Education Preparation Standards revised; ACTFL OPI Advanced Low required — MDE adopted revised Bilingual Education Preparation Standards. Standard 1.1 — flagged by MDE as the most significant change from the 2004 standards — requires candidates to demonstrate ACTFL Oral Proficiency Interview at Advanced Low or higher in BOTH English and the target language. This grounds the schema's `bilingual.requirements.languageProficiency: true`.
- 2018-01-01: Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Michigan adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in 2018, administered by MDE. The program recognizes high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and one or more additional languages.
- 2018-01-01: PK-12 Professional Knowledge and Skills standards adopted — MDE adopted the PK-12 Standards for the Preparation of Teachers (Professional Knowledge and Skills), which explicitly enumerate `linguistic` diversity and contain multiple operative references to `English learners` and `English language learners`. Subsequent revisions through 2024 retained and strengthened this language. Grounds the `professionalStandardsMentions.linguistic: true` and `.el: true` flips from the 2019 baseline.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.

## Minnesota (MN)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/mn/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Minnesota offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is a standalone teaching license. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 8.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2014.

Bilingual notes: Rule 8710.4150 — bilingual/bicultural is an add-on requiring a prerequisite license (elementary or 5–12/7–12 in math, science, social studies, or health). Subp. 4 enumerates 9 competency areas. Subp. 3 requires ACTFL advanced oral + advanced written, or schooling conducted in the target language. MTLE Bilingual exists but is not uniformly required for completers of MN-state-approved programs (PELSB Compliance Manual FY25, effective 2023-08-01).

ELD notes: Rule 8710.4400 — ESL is its own licensure field with its own student-teaching requirement. Subp. 3 enumerates 10 competency areas (A–J); subp. 3a requires ≥100 hrs field-based experience plus a 12-week full-time student-teaching placement spanning K–6, 5–8, and 9–12.

SEI notes: Rule 8710.2000 Standard 4.A names the MN English Language Development Standards Framework; all licensed teachers must understand it, but this does not rise to a sheltered-instruction mandate of the AZ/CA/MA/NV kind.

History:
- 1980-04-25: Minnesota Educational Equity for Limited English Proficient Students Act (Ch. 580, Laws of 1980) — Minnesota's first statewide EL statute (codified initially at Minn. Stat. §§ 124.273, then renumbered into §§ 124D.59-.65) committed state aid to districts operating Educational Programs for English Learners (EPELs). The 1980 act made participation voluntary for districts but tied state funding to identification, language assessment, and instructional services for ELs — establishing the funding-and-accountability architecture that the 2014 LEAPS Act later modernized. Districts retained discretion over program model (TBE, dual-language, ESL, sheltered), consistent with Minnesota's locally-controlled school-governance tradition.
- 2014-05-16: LEAPS Act enacted; state Seal of Biliteracy authorized — The Learning English for Academic Proficiency and Success (LEAPS) Act (2014 Minn. Laws ch. 272) reorganized Minnesota's EL framework and authorized the state Seal of Biliteracy. The seal language was subsequently codified at Minn. Stat. 120B.022 subd. 1b by 1Sp2015 c 3 art 2 s 2 and amended through 2024.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2022-01-01: Rule 8710.2000 (Standards of Effective Practice) revised to name MN ELD Standards Framework — PELSB's revision of Rule 8710.2000 Standard 4.A explicitly names "Minnesota's English Language Development Standards Framework," strengthening the textual basis for `professionalStandardsMentions.el: true`. Standards 1.A, 1.D, 1.H, 1.I, 2.A, 4.E, 4.F, and 5.E carry diverse/cultural/linguistic language.
- 2023-08-01: MTLE content/pedagogy/basic-skills tests no longer required for MN program completers — Per the PELSB FY25 Licensure Compliance Manual, completers of Minnesota-state-approved licensure programs are no longer required to pass MTLE content, pedagogy, or basic-skills tests effective 2023-08-01. This grounds `bilingual.requirements.test: null` and `eld.requirements.test: null`: the MTLE Bilingual and MTLE ESL exams exist but are not uniformly required.

## Mississippi (MS)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ms/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Mississippi does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 3.1% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards do not explicitly reference any of: diverse, cultural, linguistic, or English learner.
- Uses ELPA21 (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2019.

Bilingual notes: MDE does not offer a bilingual education endorsement. Appendix A of the K-12 Educator Licensure Guidelines (Dec 2025) lists Praxis-route foreign-language endorsements (Spanish, French, etc.) but no bilingual-education credential.

ELD notes: 177 — English as a Second Language (K-12) is added to a valid Mississippi license either by passing the Praxis Subject Assessment or by completing an MDE-approved program (Appendix A, K-12 Licensure Guidelines, Dec 2025). No standalone 18-hour coursework path exists for 177. The SEA does not impose a separate practicum on top of the approved-program route; practicum left null pending per-IHE program detail.

SEI notes: Mississippi does not require SEI training of all teachers. Only educators pursuing the 177 ESL endorsement are required to complete EL-specific preparation.

History:
- 2019-01-01: Mississippi Seal of Biliteracy adopted — MDE adopted the Mississippi Seal of Biliteracy in 2019, recognizing high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and one or more world languages. The MDE EL services page continues to link to the Seal policy.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2024-08-01: ELP assessment migration: LAS Links → ELPA21 Summative — Mississippi migrated its annual English Language Proficiency assessment from LAS Links to ELPA21 during the 2024-25 school year. The MDE ELPT page now references ELPA 21 as the contact and ties to the February 2026 Mississippi Testing Accommodations Manual; the MDE EL services page lists "Interpreting ELPA21 Score Reports" as a webinar topic. ELPA21's Spring 2025 Insider newsletter named Mississippi the consortium's "newest partner state" at AMTESOL 2025. This flips `elpAssessment.name` from "LAS Links" to "ELPA21 Summative" and `elpAssessment.consortium` from null to "ELPA21".

## Missouri (MO)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/mo/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Missouri does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 3.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2017.

ELD notes: ELL endorsement, K-12, per 5 CSR 20-400.570 (effective Aug 1, 2017): requires a valid Missouri permanent or professional teaching certificate, recommendation from a DESE-approved educator preparation program (per 5 CSR 20-400.500), 18 semester hours of content coursework (linguistics, language and culture, second language acquisition, methods, curriculum, assessment), 6 hours literacy, 3 hours psychology of the exceptional child, a 3-hour culminating clinical experience working with ELLs in elementary and secondary settings, and a qualifying score on the required exit assessment(s) per 5 CSR 20-400.310 and 5 CSR 20-400.440.

History:
- 2017-01-01: Missouri Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Missouri adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in 2017, administered by DESE. The DESE Seal of Biliteracy program now reports annual results back to 2020-21 across 127+ participating districts and includes a Distinguished Seal of Biliteracy tier.
- 2017-08-01: 5 CSR 20-400.570 ELL Certification Requirements (K-12) effective — DESE's ELL endorsement rule (5 CSR 20-400.570) took effect August 1, 2017, codifying the K-12 add-on certification: 18 hours of content coursework (linguistics, language and culture, second-language acquisition, methods, curriculum, assessment), 3 hours psychology of the exceptional child, 6 hours literacy, a 3-hour field/clinical experience, and a qualifying exit assessment. Together with 5 CSR 20-400.500 (general approved-program requirement) and 5 CSR 20-400.310 / .440 (assessments), this rule grounds the schema's `eld.requirements.{program,coursework,practicum,test}: true` codings.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2025-08-01: Missouri's Teacher Standards revised (August 2025) — DESE issued a revised "Missouri's Teacher Standards" document in August 2025 that replaces the older standards used in the 2019 baseline. The revised standards retain Standard 1.5 ("Diverse social and cultural perspectives"), Standard 2 references to diverse learners, and Standard 6.1's reference to "students whose first language is not Standard English," but do not name English learners explicitly — keeping `professionalStandardsMentions.el: false`.

Montana does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 2.4% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).

Bilingual notes: No bilingual-education endorsement on the FY2026 OPI endorsement code list. Montana offers world-language endorsements (06A ARA/ASL/CHI/FRE/GER/IRI/ITA/LAT/RUS/SPA) and tribal-language endorsements (06Z ASB/BLA/CHE/CHI/CRE/CRO/DAK/GV/KOO/SAL), plus a separate Class 7 American Indian Language and Culture Specialist license, but these are language-content credentials, not bilingual-education credentials.

ARM 10.57.301 explicitly excludes ESL K-12 from the degree-major / portfolio / PRAXIS-only / National Board substitute pathway, so completion of an OPI-approved educator preparation program with supervised teaching experience is the operative pathway (program=true, practicum=true). The state rule does not specify a freestanding coursework-hour count or a required exam at the SEA-policy level; coded null per the project's ambiguity rule (absence-from-rule is not affirmative absence).

SEI notes: Montana does not require sheltered English instruction (SEI) training for all teachers. ARM 10.58.501 (Teaching Standards) requires educator preparation programs to address ELLs and diverse cultures and languages, but does not impose a universal in-service SEI mandate.

- 2021-07-01: Montana Board of Public Education adopts Seal of Biliteracy — The Montana Board of Public Education adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in July 2021, authorizing districts to award the Seal to high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and one or more additional languages. ## Nebraska (NE)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ne/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Nebraska offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 7.3% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ELPA21 (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2020.

Bilingual notes: 92 NAC 24 §006.09 Bilingual Education endorsement (PK-12 / PK-6 / 7-12). Supplemental endorsement that requires the holder to also hold (or earn concurrently) an ESL endorsement plus a subject or field endorsement. Rule 24 mandates a minimum of 12 semester hours of methodology, content instruction, and content literacy in bilingual education programs, of which 9 hours must be taught in the target language, plus a 45-clock-hour practicum in a bilingual education program taught in the target language. The June 2024 Rule 24 Guidelines further set ACTFL Advanced-Low target-language proficiency as Standard 1. Both an approved educator-preparation program (Rule 20) and a Praxis content-test add-on pathway are available.

ELD notes: 92 NAC 24 §006.23 English As A Second Language endorsement (PK-12 / PK-6 / 7-12), Supplemental only — no standalone ESL/TESOL license. Rule 24 mandates 15 semester hours across Second Language Acquisition, English Language/Linguistics, Cross-Cultural Communication, Methods/Curriculum Design in ESL, and Assessment and Evaluation of ELLs, plus a 45-clock-hour practicum with ELL students. June 2024 Rule 24 Guidelines align the endorsement to TESOL standards. Per the NDE Educator Certification announcement of June 4, 2025, applicants who complete an approved educator preparation program are no longer required to pass the Praxis content test; a Praxis-test add-on pathway remains available for adding the endorsement. ESL is a prerequisite for the Bilingual Education endorsement.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2020-04-09: Nebraska Seal of Biliteracy adopted (LB 1042) — Nebraska Seal of Biliteracy authorized by LB 1042 (2020) and codified at Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-769; administered by NDE World Languages. Recognizes graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and at least one additional language.
- 2024-06-02: Rule 24 (92 NAC 24) endorsement framework readopted — NDE readopted Rule 24 effective 2024-06-02, refreshing the Bilingual Education (§006.09) and English As A Second Language (§006.23) endorsement specifications. Companion Rule 24 Guidelines (June 2024) align ESL to TESOL standards and set ACTFL Advanced-Low as the bilingual target-language proficiency floor.
- 2025-06-04: Praxis content-test waiver for approved-program completers — NDE Educator Certification announced that effective June 4, 2025 candidates completing an approved Nebraska educator-preparation program no longer need to pass the Praxis content test for endorsement; a Praxis-test add-on pathway remains available for adding endorsements without an approved program. Reflected in eld.requirements.test=false (program completers' default path).
- 2026-05-08: Re-verified against current NDE sources — Confirmed Rule 24 §006.09 / §006.23 endorsement coursework, practicum, and language-proficiency requirements; ELPA21 confirmed as Nebraska's annual ELP assessment (NDE Title III page). elPercent updated to 7.3 (NCES fall 2021). No substantive standalone/add-on changes from baseline (ESL remains supplemental-only; bilingual remains supplemental atop ESL plus a primary subject endorsement).

## Nevada (NV)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nv/
Last verified: 2026-05-07 (verified-2026)

Nevada offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 13.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-07.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2015.

Bilingual notes: NAC 391.242 (regulation T002-24, updated 2024-12-26): completion of a Department-approved bilingual preparation program OR 12 semester credits of coursework (second-language acquisition theory plus at least three of: native-language reading/language-arts methods, native-language content-area methods, second-language testing/evaluation, bilingual curriculum development, native language and culture, bilingual ed history/philosophy/theory). A Praxis language exam in the native language (e.g., Praxis Spanish) must be passed prior to issuance of the endorsement.

ELD notes: Branded as ELAD (English Language Acquisition and Development) since the late-2010s rename from the prior TESL endorsement. NAC 391.237: 11 semester hours of credit (3 each in language acquisition theory, methods for English learners, and assessment of English learners; 2 in elementary or secondary EL policies) plus a 1-semester-hour practicum (≥25 classroom hours). No exam gate. A separate Specialist in ELAD endorsement adds coursework in cultural/linguistic diversity foundations and program leadership.

SEI notes: The phase-in language reported in the 2019 baseline (early childhood/elementary 2020, middle/secondary 2021) did not produce a universal mandate. As of 2026 NAC Chapter 391 contains no general requirement that all teachers obtain ELAD or any EL-related endorsement; ELAD is a voluntary specialization.

History:
- 2015-06-09: Nevada Seal of Biliteracy enacted (AB 224, 2015) — Nevada Assembly Bill 224 (2015 session, signed 2015-06-09) created the State Seal of Biliteracy under NRS 388.5965, recognizing high school graduates proficient in English plus one or more additional languages.
- 2019-07-01: Phase-in of EL endorsement for new teachers did not produce universal mandate — The 2019 baseline reported a phase-in requiring all new early-childhood/elementary teachers (2020) and middle/secondary teachers (2021) to obtain an EL endorsement. As of 2026 NAC ch. 391 contains no general mandate that all teachers hold ELAD or any EL-related endorsement; the phased rule did not result in a universal credential requirement. Captured here so the 2019 expectation is searchable against the 2026 state of regulation.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2024-12-26: NAC 391 endorsements update (regulation T002-24) — Permanent regulation T002-24 amended NAC ch. 391 effective 2024-12-26, including the bilingual education endorsement requirements at NAC 391.242 and confirming the Praxis native-language proficiency exam (NAC 391.059) as a precondition for issuance. The TESL → ELAD branding is reflected throughout NAC 391.237.
- 2026-05-07: Re-verified against current NDE sources — Confirmed Nevada's rename of TESL → ELAD (English Language Acquisition and Development) under NAC 391.237. Bilingual.program null → true (NAC 391.242 names an approved program pathway); bilingual.test null → true (T002-24, effective 2024-12-26, requires a Praxis language exam prior to issuance). The 2019 'SEI phase-in' note retired — ELAD remains a voluntary specialization, not a universal mandate. elPercent 17.1 → 13.8 (NCES fall 2021; NCES flags NV's drop as the largest 2011–2021 negative change nationally).

## New Hampshire (NH)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nh/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

New Hampshire does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 2.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2020.

Bilingual notes: NH has no bilingual / dual-language educator endorsement in Ed 506 or Ed 507. Bilingual and dual-language are referenced in Ed 507.17 only as Language Instruction Educational Program (LIEP) types an ESOL teacher must understand, not as separate NH credentials.

ELD notes: Ed 507.17 (eff. 8-11-23) governs ESOL teacher licensure K-12. Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree, qualify through an approved program or an Ed 505.01–505.06 alternative, demonstrate oral and written English language proficiency for ELs, and provide evidence of second-language study (≥2 college semesters, ≥6 months residency abroad, or native/heritage speaker). Six competency domains (language as a system, language development, culture in student learning, methods, assessment, professionalism) are required via combined academic and supervised practical experiences. NH's competency-based system does not require a specific content-area test in rule; `test` left null.

SEI notes: No statewide SEI training mandate for all teachers. NH places EL responsibility on ESOL-endorsed teachers per Ed 507.17 and on collaborative classroom practice.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2020-09-01: NH Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Commissioner of Education Frank Edelblut approved adoption of the Seal of Biliteracy in New Hampshire in September 2020, with State Board of Education support. Students became eligible to earn the seal beginning spring 2021; the award appears on the high school diploma along with a state-issued certificate.
- 2023-08-11: Ed 507.17 ESOL Teacher rule readopted — NH State Board readopted Ed 507.17 effective 8-11-23, restructuring the ESOL teacher competencies into six domains (language as a system; language development; culture; methods; assessment; professionalism) and codifying explicit requirements for English language proficiency in oral/written domains plus second-language study experience. Approved-program or Ed 505.01–505.06 alternative pathway is required.
- 2026-05-08: Refreshed against current SEA sources (verified-2026) — Re-verified against current Ed 500 administrative rules (Ed 505.03 professional standards; Ed 507.17 ESOL teacher), the NHED Seal of Biliteracy program page, NH/WIDA identification guidance, and NCES Table 204.20. Standards refresh added cultural and linguistic flags. ELD requirement flags moved from null to true for program/coursework/practicum/languageProficiency, reflecting Ed 507.17 text. Seal of Biliteracy confirmed adopted in 2020. EL share unchanged at 2.8% (NCES fall 2021).

## New Jersey (NJ)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nj/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

New Jersey offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 8.2% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2016.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual/Bicultural Education endorsement (code 1480) under N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.5. Add-on to a CE, CEAS, or standard NJ instructional certificate. CEAS path: complete a Department-approved bilingual/bicultural preparation program. CE path: 12 credit hours of formal instruction. Target-language proficiency required via a Department-approved nationally recognized oral/written test (or equivalent undergrad/graduate education in the target language).

ELD notes: English as a Second Language endorsement (code 1475) under N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.6. Add-on to an underlying NJ instructional certificate. Path A: Department-approved NJ college/university preparation program. Path B: 15 credit hours of formal instruction across seven topic areas. Department-approved nationally recognized test of oral and written English proficiency required. languageProficiency=false because the ESL endorsement is not premised on a non-English target language; the proficiency requirement is English.

SEI notes: No statewide SEI mandate for general classroom teachers. NJ requires ESL teachers to hold an ESL endorsement; LEAs serving 10+ multilingual learners must offer one period daily of ESL by a certified teacher (N.J.S.A. 18A:6-38; N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.6).

History:
- 1975-01-06: New Jersey Bilingual Education Act enacted (P.L. 1974, c. 197) — P.L. 1974, c. 197, codified at N.J.S.A. 18A:35-15 to -26, required any school district enrolling 20 or more EL students of the same native language to operate a full bilingual education program in that language and English, plus an ESL component for any EL student regardless of language threshold. New Jersey was among the earliest states to mandate bilingual instruction by statute (after Massachusetts 1971, New Mexico 1973, Texas 1973, Illinois 1973). The 1975 statute remains the legal backbone of NJ's bilingual/bicultural and ESL endorsements (N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.5 and -11.6) and of the 20-student program-trigger threshold the State still enforces.
- 2016-01-19: New Jersey State Seal of Biliteracy enacted (P.L. 2015, c. 303) — Governor signed P.L. 2015, c. 303 on January 19, 2016, creating the New Jersey State Seal of Biliteracy administered by NJDOE. First seals awarded in the 2016-17 school year.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-08: Re-verified against current NJDOE sources — Re-confirmed N.J.A.C. 6A:9B-11.5 (Bilingual/Bicultural endorsement) and 6A:9B-11.6 (ESL endorsement) as add-on-only credentials atop a primary NJ instructional certificate; both offer an approved-program (CEAS) path and a coursework path (12 credits bilingual / 15 credits ESL) with a Department-approved test. NJ's bilingual program statute (N.J.S.A. 18A:35-15 et seq.) continues to require districts with 20+ ELs of the same native language to operate a bilingual education program. ELP assessment remains WIDA ACCESS for ELLs. elPercent set to 8.2 (NCES fall 2021). No substantive credential structure change from baseline.

## New Mexico (NM)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nm/
Last verified: 2026-05-07 (verified-2026)

New Mexico offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 18.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-07.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2014.

Bilingual notes: Under 6.64.10 NMAC: initial Level 1 candidates complete 24-36 semester hours in bilingual education AND pass the bilingual education licensure exam (6.60.5 NMAC); existing license holders add 12 semester hours plus the licensure exam. Native-language proficiency is regulated separately at 6.64.10.9 NMAC: at least an eighth-grade level of oral and written proficiency in the target non-English language. NMPED-facing materials describe the Spanish-language route as Prueba (the Praxis Spanish proficiency exam). Native American / Indigenous language teachers may instead pursue the 520 Native American Language and Culture (NALC) certificate under 6.63.14 NMAC, which substitutes tribal verification of language and cultural competence for the standard licensure exam.

ELD notes: TESOL endorsement under 6.64.11 NMAC. Initial Level 1: 24 semester hours plus PRAXIS English to Speakers of Other Languages (5362). Existing license: pass PRAXIS plus 12 semester hours, OR 24 hours alone. The English language proficiency examination is required only for international reciprocal license holders (6.64.11.8.D); domestic candidates have no language-proficiency exam gate.

SEI notes: NM does not have a universal SEI / EL-instruction endorsement mandate. The bilingual and TESOL endorsements remain voluntary specializations under NMAC Title 6. A 2019 bill to require all new teachers to hold bilingual or TESOL did not become law. Context: the consolidated Yazzie/Martinez v. State of New Mexico litigation (2014 filing, 2018 ruling that NM is failing to provide sufficient education to ELs and Native American students) has driven a multi-year remedial action plan; plaintiffs filed objections to the State's November 2025 Comprehensive Remedial Action Plan in February 2026, citing inter alia the persistent shortage of bilingual-endorsed teachers. As of 2026-05-07 no statutory or regulatory universal EL-teaching mandate has been enacted.

History:
- 1973-04-05: New Mexico Bilingual Multicultural Education Act enacted (NM Laws 1973, ch. 137) — New Mexico became the second state (after Massachusetts in 1971) to mandate bilingual education by statute. The Bilingual Multicultural Education Act (BMEA), now codified at NMSA 1978 §§ 22-23-1 to 22-23-6, requires the State to fund Bilingual Multicultural Education Programs (BMEPs) for EL students and Native American students whose home language is not English. The BMEA is the legal foundation for NM's bilingual endorsement and the BMEP program structure that the 2018 Yazzie/Martinez ruling later found the State was inadequately funding. The act was significantly amended in 2003-2004 (HB 212 / SB 219) to broaden the definition of eligible students.
- 2014-03-05: New Mexico State Seal of Bilingualism-Biliteracy enacted — NM Laws 2014, ch. 46 (Senate Bill 159) created the State Seal of Bilingualism-Biliteracy. NMPED rules at 6.32.2 NMAC implement the program; first awards issued to the high school class of 2016.
- 2018-07-20: Yazzie/Martinez ruling — NM failing EL and Native students — Consolidated Yazzie v. State and Martinez v. State litigation (filings 2014) culminated in the First Judicial District Court ruling that New Mexico is failing to provide a sufficient education to ELs, Native American students, and students with disabilities. The ruling has driven multi-year remedial-plan oversight that continues to shape NM's bilingual/TESOL teacher pipeline policy. Plaintiffs filed objections to the State's November 2025 Comprehensive Remedial Action Plan in February 2026.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-07: Re-verified against current NMPED sources — Standards.linguistic and .el both corrected to false — 6.69.4 NMAC (the general teacher competencies) contains zero mentions of EL/ELL/English learner/second language/bilingual, and the word 'linguistic' does not appear. elPercent 16.3 → 18.8 (NCES fall 2021). Notes expanded with Yazzie/Martinez v. State of New Mexico litigation and remediation context through plaintiffs' February 2026 objections to the State's November 2025 remedial action plan.

## New York (NY)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ny/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

New York offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 9.7% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses NYSESLAT (state-specific assessment).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2013.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual Education Extension: add-on only, attached to a valid base certificate. Approved program requires coursework in six content areas, ≥50 clock hours of college-supervised field experience, and the Bilingual Education Assessment (BEA), which doubles as the language-proficiency instrument for the language other than English.

ELD notes: Branded ESOL in OTI certification listings and TESOL in higher-ed program names. Standalone classroom-teacher certificate (CST 116 ESOL) plus supplementary pathway for already-certified teachers. Programs (Fall 2024+) require ≥100 clock hours of field experience and ≥70 school days of student teaching with ELL students. 12 LOTE semester hours required as coursework precondition but not as a target-language proficiency demonstration.

SEI notes: No universal SEI/EL credential mandate. CR Part 154 requires general classroom teachers of ELLs to dedicate 15% of CTLE clock hours to language acquisition addressing the needs of ELLs — a continuing-education obligation, not a credential mandate.

History:
- 1974-08-29: Aspira v. Board of Education of the City of New York consent decree (S.D.N.Y.) — ASPIRA of New York and Puerto Rican parents settled their 1972 class action against the New York City Board of Education with a consent decree that became the country's first court-ordered bilingual-education program of any scale. The decree required NYC to identify Spanish-speaking ELs and provide a Transitional Bilingual Education program (Spanish-language content instruction plus intensive ESL) for any student whose ability to participate effectively in English was below grade level. Aspira's compliance regime was the operational model that NYSED later codified for the state in CR Part 154 and remains the doctrinal touchstone for NYC's bilingual-extension teacher demand.
- 2003-05-01: NYSESLAT introduced as the state ELP assessment — New York adopted the New York State English as a Second Language Achievement Test (NYSESLAT) as its annual ELP assessment in 2003. NY has never been a WIDA Consortium member; the companion identification screener is NYSITELL. Coded as elpAssessment.consortium=null because NYSESLAT is state-specific.
- 2012-12-17: New York State Seal of Biliteracy enacted — Chapter 416 of the Laws of 2012 (signed 2012-12-17) authorized the New York State Seal of Biliteracy (NYSSB) administered by NYSED's Office of Bilingual Education and World Languages. First seals issued 2013-14. Coded as sealOfBiliteracy.year=2013 to reflect the first-award year.
- 2014-09-23: CR Part 154 Multilingual Learner / ELL regulations adopted — Board of Regents adopted revised Commissioner's Regulations Part 154 (Sept. 2014, effective school year 2015-16) governing services for ELLs/MLs, including the requirement that general classroom teachers of ELLs dedicate 15% of CTLE clock hours to language acquisition. CR Part 154 (not a new credential) is the operative ELL service mandate; underpins the sei notes.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-08: Re-verified against current NYSED sources — Re-confirmed Bilingual Education Extension as add-on-only with BEA exam doubling as language-proficiency instrument; ESOL/TESOL Classroom Teacher (CST 116) confirmed as standalone certificate with supplementary pathway. New Fall 2024 program-registration requirements (≥100 clock hrs field experience; ≥70 school days student teaching with ELLs) reflected in eld.notes. Standards.el coded false against the 2011 NY Teaching Standards general document (consistent with §3b guidance: keep 'el' against the general standards, not ESOL specialty rules). elPercent updated to 9.7 (NCES fall 2021).

## North Carolina (NC)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nc/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

North Carolina offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 8.0% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2015.

Bilingual notes: NC has no separate 'bilingual education' teaching license. The Elementary (K-6) Second Language add-on (valid for full-time assignments in grades 6 and below) and the K-12 'Other Second Languages' world-language licenses are the closest analogs. NC operates 300+ Dual Language/Immersion programs in 8 languages, staffed by teachers who hold content-area licenses plus appropriate language qualifications.

ELD notes: ESL is offered both as a K-12 standalone license (Special Subjects) and as a K-6 add-on to Elementary licensure. Approved educator preparation program (traditional or alternative) is the route to licensure; Praxis II ESL has been the state-required licensure exam for this area since 2003 (current administration via Pearson/ETS per SBE policy LICN-003).

History:
- 2008-06-05: NC Professional Teaching Standards adopted (still operative) — The State Board of Education adopted the NC Professional Teaching Standards in 2007 (revised 2008) and they remain the operative standards document. Standard II ("diverse population of students"), Standard IV references to language proficiency, and pervasive cultural-diversity language ground the schema's `professionalStandardsMentions.{diverse, cultural, linguistic}: true`. The standards do not name "English learner" or "EL" explicitly, holding `el: false`.
- 2015-01-01: North Carolina adopts Seal of Biliteracy (Global Languages Endorsement) — NC adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in 2015, implemented as the Global Languages Endorsement on the high school diploma. Recognizes graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and at least one other world language. Per the schema, this is a student-side credential and is recorded as context — the closest teacher-side analog (K-6 "Second Language" add-on) remains separate.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.

## North Dakota (ND)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/nd/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

North Dakota offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. - Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2019.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual education endorsement (NDAC code 24500) — ELD endorsement requirements plus methods of teaching bilingual education and 16 semester hours in a language other than English OR documented proficiency in a language other than English.

ELD notes: English Learner (EL) Endorsement (NDAC code 24000) — 16 semester hours across foundations/multicultural ed, linguistics, methods of teaching ESL, assessment of culturally diverse students, and field experience. Praxis ESOL is an alternative pathway in lieu of full coursework. ND is a WIDA member; the state ELP assessment is WIDA ACCESS for ELLs. ND adopted the Seal of Biliteracy in 2019 (NDSB, operated by NDDPI). Schema does not currently have dedicated fields for ELP assessment or Seal of Biliteracy; these facts are recorded here and in sources/ND/2026-05-08/changes-from-baseline.md.

History:
- 2019-09-01: North Dakota Seal of Biliteracy adopted — NDDPI adopted the North Dakota State Seal of Biliteracy in 2019, recognizing high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English plus one or more additional languages. Operated by NDDPI; first awards issued the 2019-20 school year.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-08: Re-verified against current ND ESPB and NDDPI sources — Re-confirmed NDAC ch. 67.1-02-03 EL and Bilingual endorsement requirements (16 sem. hrs. + Praxis ESOL alternative), ND ESPB adoption of InTASC Model Core Teaching Standards (Aug. 2015 final), and NDDPI's continued WIDA membership using ACCESS for ELLs. elPercent set to 3.3 (NCES Table 204.20, fall 2021). No substantive credential changes from baseline.

## Ohio (OH)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/oh/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Ohio offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 3.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses OELPA (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2017.

Bilingual notes: Two standard routes: a Bilingual Education multi-age standalone license, or a Bilingual Education endorsement on a primary teaching license. Both require completion of an approved teacher-preparation program. No OAE content exam currently exists for Bilingual Education. A Bilingual Education supplemental license (no exam, no approved program) is available for up to 3 years as a bridge to the standard route.

ELD notes: Two standard routes: a TESOL multi-age standalone license, or a TESOL endorsement on a primary teaching license. Both require an approved teacher-preparation program and the Ohio Assessments for Educators (OAE) TESOL content exam. A Supplemental TESOL license is also available (test only, no approved program), valid for 1 year and renewable up to 3 years total.

History:
- 2016-06-14: Seal of Biliteracy authorized by Substitute SB 3 — Ohio General Assembly enacted Substitute Senate Bill 3 (131st GA, 2016) authorizing a State Seal of Biliteracy. Program launched in the 2017–18 academic year for the Class of 2018 graduates; sealofbiliteracy.org records adoption as 2017-03-16.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2023-07-04: ODE renamed Ohio Department of Education and Workforce (ODEW) — House Bill 33 (FY24-25 biennial budget, signed 2023-07-04) reorganized and renamed the Ohio Department of Education to the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce. The education.ohio.gov domain continues to resolve and current SEA pages display the ODEW banner. Structural change only; EL-related teacher credentialing requirements were not altered.
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Re-verified bilingual + TESOL pathway structure against current ODEW guidance and OAC 3301-13-11 OELPA mandate. elPercent updated to 3.8% (NCES Digest 2023, Table 204.20, Fall 2021). Filled previously-null requirements.coursework/practicum=true for both bilingual and ELD reflecting approved-program structure. ELPA21 / OELPA confirmed.

## Oklahoma (OK)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ok/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Oklahoma does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 9.3% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2020.

Bilingual notes: Oklahoma does not offer a Bilingual Education teacher credential. OSDE recognizes Transitional Bilingual (IS1) and Dual Language / Two-way Immersion (IS2) as LEA-level program delivery models, but neither is a teacher endorsement. The OSDE Full Competencies document lists ESL but no Bilingual Education subject-area competency.

ELD notes: ESL (PK-12) endorsement, added via OSAT subject-area test 177. OSDE publishes ESL subject-matter competencies (Language, Culture, Planning/Implementation, Assessment, Professionalism). The candidate English-fluency expectation in competency E.5 is not a non-English language proficiency requirement. program/coursework/practicum coded null because OEQA does not publish per-endorsement approved-program or credit-hour requirements that we could verify directly.

SEI notes: OEQA State Requirement 1 requires every EPP to choose one of two pathways for all candidates: novice-high foreign-language proficiency OR knowledge/skills to address Emergent Bilingual (English Learner) students. EPPs choose the pathway, not individual teachers, so this is not a per-teacher SEI mandate. OSDE EL FAQ 2025 also acknowledges that some LEAs operate without a dedicated EL teacher.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2020-09-01: Oklahoma Seal of Biliteracy established — OSDE established the Oklahoma Seal of Biliteracy in September 2020 under 70 O.S. § 11-103.2 and OAC 210:10-1-16, making Oklahoma the 40th state plus DC to adopt. Two levels are awarded: Gold (intermediate-mid) and Platinum (advanced-low).
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Re-verified ESL endorsement (OSAT 177) as the sole EL-related credential; no Bilingual credential. Confirmed Seal of Biliteracy adoption (2020), WIDA/ACCESS membership, and refreshed professionalStandardsMentions to true for cultural/linguistic/el based on OEQA's adopted InTASC Standards (OAC 210:20-9-152) and State Requirement 1's explicit Emergent Bilingual (EL) pathway. elPercent updated to 9.3 (NCES Fall 2021).

## Oregon (OR)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/or/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Oregon offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 9.5% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ELPA21 (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2016.

Bilingual notes: Two distinct add-ons: Bilingual Specialization (ACTFL OPI/OPIc Advanced Mid+ only) and Dual Language Specialization (Commission-approved program + transcripts + language proficiency exam). Schema rolls up to the broadest pathway (Bilingual Specialization), which is exam-only.

ELD notes: ESOL is a PCR (Program Completion Report) pathway endorsement: approved program is the gating credential. ORELA ESOL test is the Commission-adopted subject-matter measure; Multiple Measures-ESOL worksheet (2024) lets EPPs document equivalent competency via coursework + clinical observations + partial test score, but does not remove the test as the default.

History:
- 2016-04-14: Oregon Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Oregon adopted a State Seal of Biliteracy on 2016-04-14 (per sealofbiliteracy.org/state/or/). Awarded to graduating high school students who demonstrate proficiency in English plus one or more additional languages.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2023-11-01: TSPC endorsement and specialization rules effective — Teacher Standards and Practices Commission rules governing Adding Endorsements and Adding Specializations took effect 2023-11-01. ESOL remains a Program Completion Report endorsement; Bilingual Specialization continues as the broadest pathway requiring ACTFL OPI/OPIc Advanced Mid+ but no approved program; Dual Language Specialization requires an approved program.
- 2024-06-01: Multiple Measures-ESOL endorsement testing option approved — TSPC approved a Multiple Measures-ESOL Endorsement Testing Option Worksheet (Commission approval June 2024, rev. 9/13/2024) documenting equivalent competency pathways: at least 20 semester / 30 quarter hours aligned with ESOL standards plus practicum or completion of a TSPC-approved ESOL program.
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Re-verified Bilingual and Dual Language Specializations and the ESOL endorsement against current TSPC rules (effective 2023-11-01) and ORELA Test Guide (rev. 3/2025). Coded bilingual program/coursework/practicum/test=false for the broadest Bilingual Specialization pathway; ESOL coursework/practicum flipped null to true. ELPA21 confirmed. elPercent updated to 9.5 (NCES Fall 2021).

## Pennsylvania (PA)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/pa/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Pennsylvania does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 4.6% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2022.

Bilingual notes: PDE does not issue a bilingual or dual-language certification. State regulation 22 Pa. Code § 4.26 names 'bilingual-bicultural' as one program type a district may operate, but no credential is awarded for it.

ELD notes: ESL Program Specialist PK-12. Add-on to a PA Instructional I or II certificate (CSPG #68, rev. 7/1/2023). State-approved preparation program with field experience/student teaching with ESL students. No state ESL test (per PDE ESL FAQ).

SEI notes: No SEI-style in-service mandate. However, 22 Pa. Code § 49.13(b)(4)(i) requires all teacher preparation programs to include at least 3 credits or 90 hours addressing the instructional needs of English language learners — a pre-service requirement, not the AZ/CA/MA SEI endorsement model.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2022-01-01: Pennsylvania Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Pennsylvania adopted a State Seal of Biliteracy in 2022, awarding the seal to graduating high school students demonstrating proficiency in English and one or more additional languages.
- 2023-07-01: PDE CSPG #68 ESL Program Specialist policy revised — PDE issued the current revision of Certification Staffing Policy Guideline #68 effective 2023-07-01, clarifying that to teach ESL in a PA public school an educator must hold a PA Instructional I or II certificate plus the ESL Program Specialist PK-12 add-on (or a comparable out-of-state ESL certificate earned via a full instructional program with student teaching).
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Re-verified ESL Program Specialist as the only PDE-issued EL credential (no bilingual cert; bilingual-bicultural is a program model under 22 Pa. Code §4.26, not a credential). Filled previously-null requirements: coursework=true, practicum=true, test=false (per ESL FAQ). Flipped professionalStandardsMentions.linguistic and .el to true based on 22 Pa. Code §49.13(b)(4)(i) explicit EL pre-service requirement. WIDA/ACCESS confirmed. elPercent updated to 4.6 (NCES Fall 2021).

## Rhode Island (RI)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ri/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Rhode Island offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 12.5% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2016.

Bilingual notes: Six standalone Bilingual / Dual Language Education certificates by grade band — Early Childhood PK-3 (§1.9.1.D), Elementary K-6 (§1.9.2.D), Middle 5-8 (§1.9.3.H), Secondary 6-12 (§1.9.4.M), and All Grades PK-12 (§1.9.5.R) — per the June 2025 RI Certification Regulations. Each requires (a) completion of a RI-Approved Program (or Credential Review / Reciprocity meeting equivalent competencies), (b) bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution, (c) 45 hours of practicum, (d) Praxis 5362 ESOL at 155 plus a language-specific test (e.g., Spanish 5195/168, French 5174/162, Mandarin 5665/164, ASL 0634/170, Latin 5601/161, German 5183/163; for all other world languages effective 2025-07-01, ACTFL OPI+WPT at Advanced Low), and (e) 'demonstrated proficiency in the first (1st) and second (2nd) languages of instruction.' Prerequisite: a valid certificate at the matching grade band, so bilingual functions as both a standalone area and an add-on layered onto base certification.

ELD notes: Two pathways. Standalone: 'English to Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL)' All Grades PK-12 certificate per §1.9.5.S — requires approved program, bachelor's, one year of practical residency (or equivalent) plus 60 hours of field experience, 45-hour practicum, and Praxis 5362 ESOL at 155. Holders of only the ESOL certificate are restricted to ELD support roles unless also certified in the relevant content area. Add-on: the MLL (Multilingual Learner) Endorsement, available to educators holding any valid RI certificate via completion of an approved MLL proficiency program at one of seven approved providers (Brown, ExcEL Leadership Academy, Rhode Island College, Rhode Island School for Progressive Education, Roger Williams, URI, RI Federation of Teachers and Health Professionals); plus 'MLL Integrated Content Teacher' grade-band variants (§§1.9.X.C) that extend an existing certificate via specific coursework in second-language acquisition, linguistics, socio-cultural studies, MLL content-based instruction, and oracy/literacy development. No second-language proficiency requirement (ESOL is the English-language-teaching credential, not a bilingual one).

SEI notes: No statewide sheltered-English-instruction mandate. RI uses content-based instruction terminology (CBI, CBI for Newcomers, CBI for SLIFE) rather than 'SEI' on the RIDE MLL/EL landing page; the 2025 Certification Regulations impose EL-instructional preparation only through specific certificates / endorsements (Bilingual/DL, ESOL, MLL Endorsement, MLL Integrated Content), not on all teachers. No requirement found analogous to AZ/CA/MA.

History:
- 2016-06-17: Rhode Island Seal of Biliteracy adopted — Rhode Island Board of Education adopted a State Seal of Biliteracy on 2016-06-17 (per sealofbiliteracy.org/state/ri/), awarded to graduating high school students demonstrating proficiency in English and one or more additional languages.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2025-06-01: RIDE Certification Regulations (June 2025) finalized — RIDE issued the Regulations Governing the Certification of Educators in Rhode Island (June 2025), the document of record behind the live Certificate Areas and Requirements index. Section 1.9.X.D.2.b explicitly requires completion of an approved program for Bilingual / Dual Language Education certificates; Section 1.9.5.S.2.a does the same for All Grades ESOL. Effective 2025-07-01, ACTFL OPI+WPT at Advanced Low replaced certain language-specific exams for 'all other world languages' in Bilingual Education.
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Re-verified Bilingual / Dual Language Education (six grade-band standalone certificates) and All Grades ESOL plus MLL endorsement / MLL Integrated Content add-on paths. Flipped bilingual.requirements.program and eld.requirements.program null to true per 2025 Cert Regs. Three of four professionalStandardsMentions flipped false to true based on RIPTS plus 2025 Cert Regs Section 1.3 explicit MLL/EL references. WIDA/ACCESS confirmed. elPercent updated to 12.5 (NCES Fall 2021; NCES notes RI as the largest positive percentage-point gain in EL representation 2011 to 2021).

## South Carolina (SC)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/sc/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

South Carolina offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 5.6% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: cultural.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2018.

Bilingual notes: On 2025-09-02 the SC State Board of Education approved a new add-on Dual Language Immersion (DLI) Teacher Endorsement (also DLI Coach and DLI Instructional Leadership endorsements). The DLI Teacher endorsement is added to an existing Initial, Professional, or Alternative Route certificate by completing two 3-semester-hour courses (Foundations of Dual Language Immersion; DLI Methods: Key Practices in Content-Based Language Instruction) with a grade of C or better. No practicum, no subject-area test, and no separately-stated language-proficiency exam are listed in the SBE-approved requirements (`languageProficiency` coded null because proficiency is implicit in the DLI role but the published endorsement requirements do not specify a proficiency screen). Coursework may be waived for completion of a comprehensive, extended sequence of professional learning approved by SCDE. There is no standalone bilingual education certification field; DLI is an add-on only.

ELD notes: Two coexisting EL credentials: (1) the ESOL field certification (Grades PK-12) — a standalone certification field; per SCDE Add-On Guidelines Section G the ESOL field 'requires specialized preparation and may not be added by method of exam,' so candidates must complete an approved preparation program or the listed coursework pathway. The pedagogy exam is Praxis PLT 5625 PreK-12 and the subject-area exam is Praxis 5362 (English to Speakers of Other Languages, qualifying score 155, per the 2025-26 Required Assessments document). The coursework pathway requires Principles and Strategies for Teaching ESOL to PK-12 Learners, Linguistics, Teaching Reading and Writing to LEP Learners, and two electives — including a Practicum in the Instruction of ESOL that may be waived with one year of successful ESOL teaching experience. (2) The ESOL Endorsement, an add-on for already-certified educators, requires Cultural and Linguistic Diversity for ESOL Educators, Principles and Strategies for Teaching ESOL to PK-12 Learners, and a 15-hour ESOL practicum (which may be embedded in the coursework). Coursework for the endorsement may be waived for an SCDE-approved sequence of professional learning.

SEI notes: South Carolina does not impose a universal Sheltered English Immersion / EL-instruction requirement on all teachers. EL-specific preparation obligations attach only to candidates seeking the ESOL field certification, the ESOL Endorsement, or the new DLI endorsements.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2025-09-02: SC SBE approves Dual Language Immersion (DLI) endorsements — South Carolina State Board of Education approves new add-on endorsements for Dual Language Immersion: DLI Teacher (two required 3-semester-hour courses), DLI Coach, and DLI Instructional Leadership. This is the first SCDE-issued bilingual-program credential. Promotes `bilingual.offered` from false to true and `bilingual.addOn` from false to true.
- 2026-05-08: Phase 2 verification (verified-2026) — Refreshed against current SCDE sources: Add-On Guidelines (ESOL field cert + ESOL endorsement), the September 2025 DLI endorsements, the 2025-26 Required Assessments document (Praxis 5362 + PLT 5625), and the NIET Teaching Standards 4.0 rubric used in Expanded ADEPT. ELD requirements refined from baseline `null`s to the explicit values now documented (program, coursework, practicum, and test all required somewhere in the ESOL pathway). Professional standards mentions revised: the NIET 4.0 rubric has no explicit 'diverse,' 'linguistic,' or EL/ESOL references, only 'cultural.' EL-population figure updated to NCES Digest 2023 Table 204.20 (fall 2021).
