## Tennessee (TN)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/tn/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Tennessee does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2024, 9.0% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ELPA21 (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2018.

ELD notes: ESL endorsement codes 488 (K-8), 489 (6-12), 490 (PreK-12). Praxis 5362 required (Professional Assessments Policy 5.105). Two pathways: traditional EPP-approved program, or TDOE's no-cost Additional Endorsement Program for already-licensed teachers (asynchronous coursework + Praxis), authorized under Educator Licensure Policy 5.502 (revised Feb 2025). ESL programs minimum 18 hours, 6 hours of college-level world language, aligned to TESOL P-12 Standards (Policy 5.505 §English as a Second Language). Practicum coded null because Policy 5.505 does not enumerate clinical/practicum hours separately for ESL — set by EPPs. 2024 update: TDOE moved EL assessment from WIDA/ACCESS to ELPA21 effective July 1, 2024 (first ELPA21 Summative Feb 5, 2025) and adopted ELPA21 ELD Standards in place of WIDA 2020. EL share rose from 4.6% (2019 baseline) to ~9% (2024 TDOE figure, 93,433 students).

SEI notes: Rule 0520-01-19-.03(8) requires annual ESL training only for teachers who provide Direct or Indirect ESL Services, not all teachers.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2024-07-01: ELP assessment migrated WIDA → ELPA21 — Per the May 30, 2024 SBE workshop 'English as a Second Language ELPA21 Transition' presentation, Tennessee transitioned from the WIDA ACCESS for ELLs to ELPA21 effective July 1, 2024, with the first ELPA21 Summative administration on February 5, 2025. The transition also introduced new Tennessee ELD Standards (10) aligned to the ELPA21 framework. The TDOE EL Assessments page now references ELPA21 as the operative annual ELP measure.
- 2026-05-08: Standards verified — promoted to verified-2026 — Retrieved current SBE Policy 5.505 'Literacy and Specialty Area Standards for Educator Preparation' (revised 11/21/2025) and Policy 5.502 'Educator Licensure' (revised 02/21/2025). Policy 5.505 explicitly references diverse instructional practices, students' cultural and linguistic experiences, language/linguistic diversity as a source of strength, culturally relevant and responsive instruction, and English Learners by name (e.g., 'all learners (e.g., English Learners, students with disabilities, and at-risk learners)') in general literacy and early-childhood standards applicable beyond the ESL endorsement. ESL programs are aligned to TESOL P-12 Standards and require instruction on the Tennessee EL Framework. All four professionalStandardsMentions booleans (diverse, cultural, linguistic, el) confirmed true against the current standards document.

## Texas (TX)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/tx/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Texas offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 20.2% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses TELPAS (state-specific assessment).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2013.

Bilingual notes: SBEC issues a Bilingual Education Supplemental certificate (19 TAC §233.6); a new Core/Bilingual Education Spanish with the Science of Teaching Reading: EC-Grade 6 base certificate becomes issuable Sept 1, 2028 (§233.2(f)). Required exams include the Bilingual Target Language Proficiency Test (BTLPT, #190), the Bilingual Supplemental (#164), Core Subjects EC-6 (or grade-band equivalent), and PPR or edTPA. Texas also recognizes a Bilingual Special Education Supplemental EC-12 effective Sept 1, 2027 (§233.8(a)). Practicum (clinical) experience left null as a separate flag because the EPP route bundles it; will revisit when the schema separates EPP-embedded vs. standalone practicum.

ELD notes: SBEC issues an English as a Second Language Supplemental certificate (19 TAC §233.7), required for any teacher serving emergent bilingual students in an ESL program (TEC §29.061). A Core/ESL Supplemental with the Science of Teaching Reading: EC-Grade 6 base certificate becomes issuable Sept 1, 2028 (§233.2(g)). Required exam: ESL Supplemental (#154) plus PPR or edTPA. No target-language proficiency exam is required for ESL.

SEI notes: Texas mandates bilingual or ESL services for emergent bilingual students (TEC Chapter 29 Subchapter B; 19 TAC §§89.1201, 89.1205, 89.1210), but those services are delivered by appropriately certified bilingual or ESL teachers — Texas does not impose an SEI training requirement on all classroom teachers.

History:
- 1973-06-12: Texas Bilingual Education and Training Act enacted (SB 121, 63rd Legislature) — Texas became the third state (after Massachusetts 1971 and New Mexico 1973) to mandate bilingual education by statute. SB 121 required school districts with 20 or more EL students of the same language background in the same grade level (K-3) to provide bilingual instruction, and authorized the Texas Education Agency to certify bilingual teachers. The law was substantially expanded by SB 477 (1981) — passed in the wake of the U.S. v. Texas (Civ. Action 5281) federal-court order — to cover K-elementary and to require both bilingual and ESL programs depending on enrollment thresholds. The current 19 TAC Chapter 89 framework descends from this statutory backbone.
- 1981-06-23: Castañeda v. Pickard decided by the Fifth Circuit (648 F.2d 989) — Arising out of the Raymondville, Texas ISD, the Fifth Circuit established the three-prong test that federal courts use to evaluate state and district compliance with the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974: (1) the program must be based on sound educational theory; (2) it must be implemented effectively with adequate resources and personnel; and (3) the district must evaluate the program and modify it if it is not producing results. The Castañeda standard remains the controlling EEOA test for EL programs nationwide and is the doctrinal anchor cited in the 2011 DOJ settlement with Massachusetts and the Flores v. Arizona litigation.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-08: Re-audited against current SBEC rules and NCES EL share — Re-verified against 19 TAC Chapter 233 (May 2024 update) and the TEA Bilingual/ESL Certification Pathways and Required Tests Chart. Bilingual Education Supplemental (§233.6) and ESL Supplemental (§233.7) remain the operative EL credentials; new Core/Bilingual Education Spanish and Core/ESL Supplemental base certificates with the Science of Teaching Reading become issuable Sept 1, 2028 (§233.2(f)-(g)); Bilingual Special Education Supplemental EC-12 effective Sept 1, 2027 (§233.8(a)). elPercent updated from 18 (2019 baseline) to 20.2 to align with NCES Digest Table 204.20 fall 2021.

## Utah (UT)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/ut/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Utah offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 8.3% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2015.

Bilingual notes: USBE Dual Language Immersion (DLI) Endorsement attaches to a Professional or Associate Educator License (Elementary or Secondary) and authorizes K-12 DLI and Bridge classroom assignment. Three named requirement areas: (1) Foundations of DLI — satisfied by a USBE-approved DLI prep program/minor at one of five Utah universities (BYU, Utah, USU, UVU, Weber State), a Foundations of DLI university course, or six competency-based microcredential modules; (2) DLI Clinical Experience — satisfied via the same approved program OR ≥1 year teaching in an approved DLI/Bridge program; (3) World Language Oral Proficiency — ACTFL OPI Advanced-Mid, ACTFL OPIc Advanced-Low, or a bachelor's degree from a foreign university taught in the target language. No Praxis content exam is required.

ELD notes: USBE English as a Second Language Endorsement (ADA-Compliant application 7/10/2023) is an add-on to a current Educator License, anchored to TESOL Pre-K-12 Teacher Preparation Standards. Five requirement areas — Language, Culture, Assessment, Instruction, and Family & Community Engagement (Professionalism) — each satisfied by ONE of four interchangeable demonstrations of competency: (a) university course, (b) competency-based USBE-approved LEA program, (c) Master's degree with ESL major or minor (or out-of-state ESL license), or (d) Praxis II 5362 (English to Speakers of Other Languages, passing score 149). The application does not list a practicum requirement; the underlying R277 administrative rule was not retrieved in this verification pass, so practicum is logged as unknown rather than false.

- 2026-05-08: Re-verified against current USBE sources — Re-coded both EL credentials against current USBE endorsement applications. Bilingual (DLI) Endorsement: coursework null → true and practicum null → true (DLI Clinical Experience is a named requirement area; coursework pathway is explicit on the application); test null → false (no Praxis content exam — language proficiency is via ACTFL OPI/OPIc, captured under languageProficiency). ## Vermont (VT)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/vt/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Vermont offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 2.0% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2020.

Bilingual notes: VSBPE Rule 5440-39 Bilingual Education (revised June 2018). Add-on endorsement only, layered on a base endorsement (early childhood, elementary, middle grades, special ed, ELL, science, social studies, math, or English language arts). Knowledge Standard 1.1 requires 'measurable academic language proficiency in English and a second language including listening, speaking, reading and writing skills'; the rule does not name a specific proficiency exam. Practicum required in Bilingual/Dual Language Education at the PK-6 or 7-12 level (PK-12 authorization requires a practicum at both levels). Approved-program pathway is the standard route (endorsement 39 is not on the Transcript Review list at Rule 5230).

ELD notes: VSBPE Rule 5440-40 English Language Multilingual Learner (revised August 2015, May 2022; abbreviated 'ELLML'). Five competency standards: Knowledge About Language; Multilingual Learners in the Sociocultural Context; Planning and Implementing Instruction; Assessment and Evaluation; Professionalism and Leadership. Approved Educator preparation program is the standard pathway (endorsement 40 is not on the Transcript Review list). Practicum required at PK-8 or 5-12 (PK-12 authorization requires both). Required test: Praxis II ESOL (test code 5362) per Rule 5246. Rule 5440-40 §1.2 explicitly aligns to WIDA English Language Development Standards.

SEI notes: Vermont has no general SEI/sheltered-instruction mandate for all teachers. EL instruction is delivered by educators holding endorsement 40 (ELLML); the Core Teaching Standards (5235) reference linguistic diversity but do not require EL-specific competency from every license holder.

## Virginia (VA)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/va/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Virginia offers Bilingual Education both as a standalone certification and as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 9.4% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2015.

Bilingual notes: Dual Language Endorsement adopted by VDOE effective 2025 (8VAC20-23-321 through -324). Four parallel sections cover Dual Language (English) preK-6 standalone and add-on, plus Dual Language (target language) preK-6 standalone and add-on. Approved teacher preparation program is one path; the alternate path requires specified semester hours plus elementary content / reading-for-educators assessments (English pathway) or 12 SH target language above intermediate level OR a qualifying language assessment (target-language pathway). VDOE introduced the endorsement via the August 7, 2025 webinar 'Introducing the Dual Language Endorsement and Data Management Updates.'

ELD notes: ESL preK-12 endorsement under 8VAC20-23-350. Two paths: (1) approved teacher preparation program in ESL, or (2) 24 semester hours distributed across reading & writing (6), English linguistics (3), cross-cultural education (3), second language acquisition (3), ESL methods grounded in the WIDA English Language Development Standards (3), ESL assessment (3), and electives (3). VDOE requires the Praxis English to Speakers of Other Languages test for the add-on path. Practicum requirement embedded in approved-program path but not separately enumerated in -350; coded null.

## Washington (WA)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/wa/
Last verified: 2026-05-07 (verified-2026)

Washington offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 11.4% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-07.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural, linguistic, el.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2014.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual Education endorsement governed by PESB under WAC 181-82A. Added to a teaching certificate (no standalone license). Per WAC 181-82A-204(2)(a), the route is a state-approved endorsement program addressing PESB competencies plus the WEST-E content test; field experience is at the program provider's discretion. PESB endorsement competencies (Standard 1.A) require candidates to demonstrate 'a high level of oral and written language proficiency' in the additional language of instruction 'as demonstrated by performance on a standardized assessment of language proficiency.' Post-Fall 2021 candidates are evaluated against NDLETPS (National Dual Language Education Teacher Preparation Standards).

ELD notes: English Language Learner (ELL) endorsement (PESB, 2015 competencies). Added to a teaching certificate (no standalone license). Same WAC 181-82A-204 route as Bilingual: state-approved endorsement program plus WEST-E content test; field experience at provider discretion. Unlike the Bilingual endorsement, no candidate language-proficiency gate. OSPI uses 'Multilingual/English Learner' branding in current program guidance; PESB retains the 'ELL' label on the endorsement itself.

SEI notes: Washington has no universal SEI / sheltered-instruction endorsement mandate. The Transitional Bilingual Instruction Program (TBIP, RCW 28A.180) is an OSPI-administered district program serving identified multilingual/EL students; it does not require all certificated teachers to hold an EL-related endorsement.

History:
- 1979-05-23: Washington Transitional Bilingual Instruction Program established (Ch. 95, Laws of 1979) — The Washington Legislature enacted RCW 28A.180 (originally Chapter 95, Laws of 1979) creating the Transitional Bilingual Instruction Program (TBIP) and committing state funds to districts serving EL students. Unlike the bilingual mandates in MA/NM/TX/IL/NJ, Washington's statute permits districts to choose program model — bilingual where staffing allows, ESL/sheltered instruction otherwise — and ties state funding to enrollment of identified ELs. RCW 28A.180.020 still requires OSPI to report annually on the program. OSPI rebranded the umbrella as the Multilingual Education Program in recent guidance, but the underlying TBIP statute remains the legal backbone of WA's EL services.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-07: Re-verified against current OSPI/PESB sources — Bilingual.standalone and ELD.standalone both true → false — Washington's ELL and Bilingual credentials are PESB endorsements added to a teaching certificate, not standalone licenses (WAC 181-82A). Standards.diverse and .el corrected false → true (InTASC, adopted by PESB as the role standards, explicitly enumerates 'English language learners' across Standards 1, 2, 6, 8 and references linguistic diversity; 2022 CCDEI standards add the diverse and cultural framing). TBIP renamed to Multilingual Education in OSPI guidance.

## West Virginia (WV)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/wv/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

West Virginia does not offer a bilingual education credential; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 0.8% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards do not explicitly reference any of: diverse, cultural, linguistic, or English learner.
- Uses ELPA21 (ELPA21 consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2021.

Bilingual notes: Policy 5202 (eff. 2025-01-11) lists no bilingual teaching specialization or endorsement; only ESL Pre-k-Adult appears as the EL-related credential.

ELD notes: ESL Pre-k-Adult is a standalone teaching specialization in Policy 5202 (Tbl, eff. 2025-01-11). Issuance pathways: (1) completion of a WVBE-approved EPP aligned to TESOL national standards (Policy 5100 §6.6, eff. 2023-12-11) plus the Content Specialization Praxis (Policy 5202 §10.1.c.2.A.2); or (2) additional endorsement on an existing professional teaching certificate via passing the appropriate content-proficiency exam (Policy 5202 §21.1–§21.2). Field-based and yearlong-residency clinical experiences are required by Policy 5100 §6.7.b and §6.8. No language-proficiency exam is required for ESL (those requirements are limited to ASL and the modern foreign languages).

SEI notes: No SEI mandate appears in Policy 5202, 5100, or 5310. WV relies on the ESL-endorsed specialist model rather than requiring all teachers to complete SEI coursework.

History:
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2021-03-18: West Virginia adopts the Seal of Biliteracy — Per the national Seal of Biliteracy state tracker, West Virginia adopted the Seal of Biliteracy on 2021-03-18, recognizing high school graduates who attain proficiency in English and one or more additional languages. Prior to this verification the record had `adopted: false` based on a now-stale Wikipedia table; the SoB national page confirms WV adoption.
- 2023-10-16: WVPTS reaffirmed in revised Policy 5310 — WVBE Policy 5310 (Performance Evaluation of Professional Personnel and Athletic Coaches, 126CSR142) is amended; §13.1 continues to set the West Virginia Professional Teaching Standards as five summary elements that determine 80 percent of a teacher's summative rating. None of the five elements explicitly references diverse, cultural, linguistic, or English Learner content.
- 2023-12-11: Educator preparation rules amended (Policy 5100) — WVBE Policy 5100 (Approval of Educator Preparation Programs, 126CSR114) is amended. EPPs leading to the ESL Pre-k-Adult specialization must align to the National Standards for Teachers of English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) and to the current state-approved content standards, with field-based and yearlong-residency clinical experiences required for all initial-licensure programs.
- 2025-01-11: Licensure rules amended (Policy 5202) — WVBE Policy 5202 (Minimum Requirements for the Licensure of Professional/Paraprofessional Personnel, 126CSR136) becomes effective. ESL Pre-k-Adult is retained as a teaching specialization; §18.10 articulates the ESL teacher's role with English Learners; §21.1–§21.2 allow an additional endorsement on an existing professional teaching certificate via the appropriate content-proficiency Praxis score.

## Wisconsin (WI)

URL: https://projectcert.org/states/wi/
Last verified: 2026-05-08 (verified-2026)

Wisconsin offers Bilingual Education as an add-on endorsement; ELD/ESL is available both as a standalone license and as an add-on endorsement. SEI training is not mandated for all teachers. As of 2021, 5.9% of public-school students are classified English Learners (NCES). Re-verified against current SEA sources on 2026-05-08.

- Professional teaching standards explicitly reference: diverse, cultural.
- Uses ACCESS for ELLs (WIDA Consortium member).
- Seal of Biliteracy adopted in 2015.

Bilingual notes: Bilingual-Bicultural Education (subject 1023) is a supplemental license under PI 34.078 — it requires an underlying Tier II/III/IV teaching license and is not standalone. PI 34.078(2)(b) requires proficiency in English and the target language; PI 34.078(2)(c) requires an approved program with coursework in cultural studies, foundations, theory and methodology, contrastive language study (phonology/morphology/syntax), bilingual-bicultural field experiences, and a clinical program. No state-adopted bilingual content test exists; each EPP measures English and target-language proficiency (commonly via ACTFL). The underlying primary-license content test and edTPA gate the pathway.

ELD notes: ESL (subject 1395) is a kindergarten through grade 12 teaching-area license under PI 34.047(3)(e) earned via an approved program plus assessments under PI 34.021(1)(c)-(d) (Praxis II ESOL #0360, passing 530, plus edTPA in Teaching Students of Other Languages). PI 34.052(6) creates an add-on pathway for holders of an elementary/middle school, special education, or equivalent license: the ESL credential may be added by passing the approved content knowledge test (no second approved program required). No language-proficiency exam is required of ESL candidates.

SEI notes: Wisconsin does not mandate SEI-style training for all teachers. SEI/Sheltered English/Content-Based ESL is one of several Language Instruction Educational Program models (alongside pull-out ESL, push-in ESL, and bilingual program models) districts may run, taught by ESL-licensed (1395) staff.

History:
- 1975-12-22: Wisconsin Bilingual-Bicultural Education Act enacted (Ch. 395, Laws of 1975) — Wisconsin enacted one of the strongest state bilingual mandates in the country, codified at Wis. Stat. §§ 115.95 to 115.996. Districts must operate a bilingual-bicultural education program at any school enrolling 10 or more EL students at the K-3 level, 20 or more at grades 4-8, or 20 or more at the high-school level — all of the same non-English language background. The 1975 act also established the bilingual-bicultural teacher license category that PI 34.078 (formerly PI 34.33(3)) administers today, and is the legal source of Wisconsin's status as a bilingual-program state rather than an SEI state. The statute's combination with WIDA (headquartered at UW-Madison) makes Wisconsin distinctive in the upper Midwest.
- 2015-10-01: Wisconsin Seal of Biliteracy initiated by DPI — DPI launched the Wisconsin Seal of Biliteracy in October 2015 to recognize graduating high-school students who demonstrate proficiency in English plus one or more additional languages. The program is administered by DPI rather than created by a standalone authorizing statute; districts opt in and award the seal locally.
- 2017-09-15: DPI publishes ESL/Bilingual-Bicultural/World Languages license guidance — DPI's Teacher Education, Professional Development and Licensing team issued a one-stop guidance document mapping each WI language-instruction license (ESL 1395, Bilingual-Bicultural 1023, World Language) to the program models it can be used in (sheltered/SEI, pull-out/push-in ESL, transitional/two-way/maintenance bilingual, immersion) and the educator-preparation requirements for each — including Praxis II ESOL #0360 (passing 530), edTPA, and the EPP-administered language-proficiency check (commonly ACTFL) for bilingual candidates.
- 2018-08-01: Chapter PI 34 (educator licenses) reorganized and renumbered — The Wisconsin administrative-rule re-number consolidated the educator licensing scheme. The bilingual-bicultural supplemental rule moved from PI 34.33(3) to PI 34.078; the ESL teaching-area subject moved from PI 34.30(g) to PI 34.047(3)(e); and the add-on-by-content-test pathway for ESL/world-languages was placed at PI 34.052(6). Substantive requirements (approved program, English + target-language proficiency for bilingual, content-area test for add-on) were preserved across the renumbering.
- 2019-12-01: Baseline coding (Leider, Colombo & Nerlino, 2021) — Initial coding of the SEA's bilingual, ELD/ESL, and SEI credentials, professional teaching standards, and EL-population data. Captured Oct–Dec 2019 for the EPAA 29(100) document analysis; this row is the as-of-2019 snapshot against which subsequent verifications are diffed.
- 2026-05-08: Refresh against current SEA sources (verified-2026) — Re-verified Wisconsin's record against current DPI pages and Wisconsin Administrative Code Chapter PI 34. Corrections vs. baseline: bilingual is supplemental (not standalone) under PI 34.078; ESL is available both as a standalone PI 34.047(3)(e) license and as a PI 34.052(6) content-test add-on; the operative 10 Wisconsin Educator Standards do not literally mention 'linguistic' or 'English learner,' so those professionalStandardsMentions booleans flip to false; elPercent updated to 5.9% (NCES Fall 2021).
